comparator.name: Arabische Taal en Cultuur
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum defines a complete 180-EC pathway. Year 1 is a 60-EC common foundation with four sequential Arabic-language courses, Arabic in Context, regional history and humanities/regional-studies methods. The generic normalized target offers two formal majors after year 1. Major Arabische studies is selected because it most directly continues the named programme’s Arabic-language-and-culture identity; Major Middle Eastern Studies discontinues language acquisition and is not combined with it. The selected major contains 30 EC of second-year taught courses, a 30-EC Cairo semester, 18 EC of advanced Arabic source/literature study, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The resulting pathway totals exactly 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target is Arabic Language and Culture. Of the two current formal majors, Major Arabische studies directly continues the programme’s intensive Arabic-language sequence, Arabic-source work, Cairo semester and Arabic-language thesis. Major Middle Eastern Studies explicitly ends language acquisition after year 1 and is therefore less representative of the named generic bachelor. The route was selected before assessing UCR fit.

programmes.label: Arabische Taal en Cultuur at University of Amsterdam

exception.reason: The selected UvA pathway is defined by a cumulative Arabic-language sequence: Egyptian Arabic, Arabic script, Modern Standard Arabic, grammar, vocabulary, speaking, listening, reading and writing, followed by Arabic sociolinguistics, Arabic-medium literary study, a 30-EC Cairo semester, Arabic media and source interpretation, and a 12-EC thesis that combines Arabic competence with disciplinary analysis. UCR’s current catalogue contains no Arabic-language course at any level and no course whose sustained disciplinary object is Arabic linguistics or Arabic-language literature. UCR history, politics, religion, literature and media courses can illuminate isolated regional or comparative questions, but they cannot supply the language competence on which the advanced curriculum and thesis depend. A 24-course response would therefore be a broad humanities and regional-studies programme without Arabic, not a defensible closest match to Arabic Language and Culture.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official Major Arabische studies pathway accounts for exactly 180 EC: a 60-EC common first year, a 30-EC second-year taught sequence, a 30-EC Cairo semester, 18 EC of advanced third-year Arabic source/literature study, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The alternative Major Middle Eastern Studies is not combined with it. Genuine free choice remains open rather than being populated with invented electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches Arabic speaking, listening, reading, writing, grammar or translation, and no course provides a sequence in Arabic linguistics or Arabic-language literature. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literature, MCCLITR112 Texts & Worlds, MCCLITR212 Literature & Society, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Contemporary Literatures provide transferable literary and cultural analysis; GOSHIST and GOSPOLI courses provide broad historical and political methods; GOSPHIL and GOSLAWJ courses address philosophy, religion and law; MCCMEDI and MCCCOMM courses support media and intercultural analysis. These subjects could support comparative work on society, culture and representation, but they do not establish the Arabic competence required for advanced Arabic-medium study, Arabic sources, the Cairo semester and the Arabic-focused thesis. Because the missing language sequence is the programme’s academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent Arabic Language and Culture programme.
